schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: THE INSTALL INSPECTOR AND GATE, a Recovery machine. inspector.py holds CHECKS, a list of install checks (each a 'module:function' string or a callable, functools.partial included) shaped {id,status,detail}. inspect(checks=None) runs every check with dry_run=True, writes nothing, and returns the reds: every status but already_applied, and a check that raises, its exception carried in the detail. installed(checks=None) is the gate: (False, reds) while any red stands, (True, []) once all are green. The installer's fix_reds calls each red check once with dry_run=False and no green check. The first CHECKS are the installer's install, ensure_journal_merge_driver and ensure_dev_extra.
why: Akien, 2026-11-12, verbatim: "i would say we need an install inspector and gate. then we can set up python, and once it's set up use that to detect what else with just a tool call. part of recovery and install". Measured the same day: akienasus had none of the 15 skills and no pytest, akiendell none of the 16 skills, and each was fixed by hand, because a box gets only what someone remembered to add and nothing reads what is missing. Law 3 (an install is not known until measured), Law 4 (enforced by an inspector and gate, not remembered), Law 1 (each hand-fix becomes a registered check).
invoke: `from cairn.devices.recovery.machines.install_inspector.inspector import inspect, installed, CHECKS`; the installer's main() asks installed() after fix_reds, and `--check` prints the reds and writes nothing.
how_it_learns: Not yet. It measures the box fresh each call and keeps no memory of past runs; a new install fact joins by registering a check into CHECKS, an authored act, not something it discovers.
public_interface: fix_reds(checks=None, *, run_checks=None) -> list[dict] (published by the installer, called by its main())
